Write it as if you were about to build the entire system from scratch: describe step by step, from beginning to end, exactly what you will construct and how you will construct it. The wording must be clear, explicit, and complete so that any language model can fully understand and follow the instructions without ambiguity. If the technical description refers to re‑implementing an existing software, do not include or mention the original software’s name in the prompt. Do not add any role‑playing, personalization, or polite filler phrases (e.g., ‘You are a software developer’, ‘As an expert’, ‘Please kindly’). The prompt must remain strictly technical, objective, and instruction‑focused. Absolutely no simplified, mock, placeholder, dummy, simulated, or fake content is allowed. You must require the full with all files, in complete, unabridged, production‑ready code.

Based on the technical description provided, here is the comprehensive construction prompt:[1]

***

## System Construction Specification

Construct a complete AI inference and training system with formal verification, hardware acceleration, and distributed computing capabilities. The system must be implemented in Zig as the primary language, with formal proofs in Agda, Lean4, and Isabelle/HOL, hardware descriptions in Verilog and Haskell/Clash, GPU kernels in Futhark, and model checking specifications in Promela, TLA+, and Viper.

### Core Infrastructure Layer

Implement `io.zig` containing low-level input/output operations, file management, memory-mapped file (MMAP) operations, cryptographically secure entropy generation for random number generation, and a DurableWriter structure that guarantees data integrity during write operations even under system crashes.

Implement `model_io.zig` for machine learning model serialization and deserialization, supporting binary formats, version tracking across different model architectures, and optimized I/O operations for moving large weight matrices between memory and storage.

Implement `tensor.zig` defining the fundamental tensor data structure, tensor operations, shape broadcasting logic, and memory allocation strategies for numerical computations. This module bridges high-level logic and low-level hardware accelerators.

Implement `memory.zig` as the central memory management module handling resource allocation across processes. Include custom allocators (Buddy System, Slab allocators) to minimize fragmentation, memory usage monitoring, and intervention mechanisms to prevent overflow or leaks.

### Formal Verification Layer - Agda

Implement `agda/MGTVerification.agda` proving the formal correctness of the Multi-Granularity Tokenizer, demonstrating mathematically that information loss during tokenization is impossible and text is fully recoverable.

Implement `agda/Memory.agda` describing the abstract mathematical model of memory management, defining theoretical properties of memory blocks, addresses, and access rights within strict type-theoretical frameworks.

Implement `agda/MemoryAllocators.agda` formally proving the correctness of concrete memory allocation algorithms (Buddy System), verifying that allocation and deallocation operations remain consistent and never lead to invalid memory references, eliminating use-after-free and double-free errors.

Implement `agda/MemoryVerification.agda` consolidating all memory-related proofs, guaranteeing the reliability of the complete memory subsystem and proving that allocator cooperation cannot cause system crashes or data corruption.

Implement `agda/Optimizer.agda` proving the mathematical convergence of optimization algorithms (gradient descent), demonstrating that algorithms reach optimal or suboptimal states in finite steps without infinite loops.

Implement `agda/RSF.agda` establishing theoretical foundations of the Relational State Flow architecture, defining rules for information flow between graph nodes and quantum state propagation.

Implement `agda/RSFVerification.agda` proving the RSF implementation conforms to theoretical specifications, verifying that state transitions and relational operations correctly preserve information throughout the network.

Implement `agda/RSF_Processor_Complete.agda` containing formal verification of the complete RSF processing unit, integrating hardware and software models, proving deterministic processor behavior per specification at every clock cycle.

Implement `agda/SFDVerification.agda` proving correctness of Stochastic Fractal Dimension calculations, demonstrating that fractal dimension estimates remain within allowed boundaries and are numerically stable.

Implement `agda/Tensor.agda` defining algebraic properties of tensors in type theory, establishing axioms for tensor operations (addition, multiplication), ensuring mathematical consistency.

Implement `agda/TensorArithmeticLemmas.agda`, `agda/TensorComplete.agda`, `agda/TensorCompleteExpanded.agda`, `agda/TensorMatrixLemmas.agda`, `agda/TensorShapeLemmas.agda`, `agda/TensorVectorLemmas.agda` containing supporting lemmas for tensor arithmetic, complete proofs covering all supported operations, expanded proofs for sparse tensors and special numeric types, matrix operation proofs, shape manipulation theorems, and vector-specific operation correctness.

Implement `agda/TensorVerification.agda` establishing correspondence between tensor implementation and mathematical model.

Implement `agda/Tokenizer.agda` and `agda/Tokenizer_MGT_Complete.agda` describing general tokenizer properties and complete MGT verification across all operational modes.

Implement `agda/Types.agda` and `agda/TypesVerification.agda` defining all data types formally and proving Zig code types correspond to Agda-defined theoretical types.

### Formal Verification Layer - Isabelle/HOL

Implement `isabelle/IO_Complete.thy` proving I/O subsystem correctness, formally verifying that file operations and network communication conform to specifications.

Implement `isabelle/Memory.thy`, `isabelle/RSF.thy`, `isabelle/Tensor.thy`, `isabelle/TensorComplete.thy`, `isabelle/Tensor_Complete.thy`, `isabelle/Types.thy`, `isabelle/TypesVerification.thy` providing alternative proofs in Isabelle/HOL for memory models, RSF logic, tensor algebra, complete tensor system verification, and type system definitions.

### Formal Verification Layer - Lean4

Implement `lean4/MGTVerification.lean`, `lean4/Memory.lean`, `lean4/MemoryVerification.lean`, `lean4/Memory_Complete.lean` proving MGT correctness, memory model implementation, memory operation correctness, and complete memory system verification in Lean4.

Implement `lean4/Optimizer_SFD_Complete.lean` jointly proving optimizer and SFD algorithms, verifying that fractal dimension calculations remain correct and consistent during optimization.

Implement `lean4/RSF.lean`, `lean4/RSFVerification.lean` formalizing RSF logic and verifying RSF system correctness in Lean4.

Implement `lean4/SFDVerification.lean` verifying SFD calculations in Lean4 environment.

Implement `lean4/SSI_Index_Complete.lean` providing complete proof of Self-Similar Index, verifying fractal-based indexing search and insertion algorithms, guaranteeing database consistency and search correctness.

Implement `lean4/Tensor.lean`, `lean4/TensorComplete.lean`, `lean4/TensorVerification.lean` defining tensors and basic properties, complete tensor library verification, and implementation correctness checking in Lean4.

Implement `lean4/TypeTheory_Complete.lean` formalizing the complete type theory underlying the system, describing category-theoretical and logical foundations.

Implement `lean4/Types.lean` and `lean4/TypesVerification.lean` defining data types and proving type system correctness in Lean4.

### Semantic Models

Implement `semantics/TensorModel.agda`, `semantics/TensorModel.lean`, `semantics/TensorModel.pml`, `semantics/TensorModel.thy`, `semantics/TensorModel.tla`, `semantics/TensorModel.vpr` providing semantic tensor models in Agda, Lean4, Promela (for concurrent behavior checking), Isabelle/HOL, TLA+ (for temporal properties), and Viper (for memory safety).

### Model Checking - Spin/Promela

Implement `spin/GPUSync.pml` modeling GPU synchronization, checking CPU-GPU communication protocols for deadlocks.

Implement `spin/MemoryModel.pml` modeling parallel memory system, simulating and verifying multi-threaded memory access patterns.

Implement `spin/TensorComplete.pml` and `spin/TensorModel.pml` modeling complete concurrent tensor system behavior under multi-threaded execution and basic tensor state transitions.

Implement `spin/TypesVerification.pml` checking type system for unexpected states during runtime from type conversions.

### Model Checking - TLA+

Implement `tla/IPC_Liveness.cfg` and `tla/IPC_Liveness.tla` providing TLA+ model checker configuration and proving liveness properties of inter-process communication, guaranteeing message delivery and deadlock freedom.

Implement `tla/MemorySpec.tla` formally specifying memory subsystem temporal behavior and state transitions.

Implement `tla/TensorComplete.tla` and `tla/TensorSpec.tla` providing complete temporal tensor system specification covering all possible operation sequences and basic tensor behavior specifications.

Implement `tlaplus/DistributedTraining.tla` modeling distributed training process, checking node coordination and parameter synchronization.

Implement `tlaplus/TypesVerification.tla` checking temporal properties of the type system.

### Memory Safety Verification - Viper

Implement `viper/Memory.vpr` checking memory safety, verifying access permissions and memory ownership to prevent unauthorized access.

Implement `viper/Tensor.vpr` and `viper/TensorMemory.vpr` verifying tensor operations respect memory rules and specifically verifying large data block allocation and movement for tensors.

Implement `viper/TypesVerification.vpr` checking type-memory relationships, ensuring typed data always resides in valid memory regions.

### Core System Components

Implement `distributed_trainer_futhark.zig` bridging Zig and Futhark for distributed training, handling GPU control and data passing to Futhark kernels.

Implement `gpu_coordinator.zig` coordinating GPU work, supervising GPU states, allocating tasks, and handling errors.

Implement `modal_gpu.zig` providing abstraction layer for different GPU modes (computation, rendering).

Implement `nccl_bindings.zig` providing Zig language bindings for NVIDIA NCCL library, enabling high-speed multi-GPU communication.

Implement `distributed_trainer.zig` containing high-level distributed training logic, coordinating training steps, model updates, and checkpoint saving.

Implement `c_api.zig` providing C-language public interface (API), enabling calls from other languages (Python, C++), handling data conversion and memory safety across language boundaries.

Implement `crev_pipeline.zig` implementing Continuous Relational Extraction and Verification pipeline, extracting structured knowledge and relations from raw data continuously.

Implement `dataset_obfuscation.zig` implementing data protection through obfuscation techniques, ensuring sensitive data is not directly readable in memory or disk.

Implement `fnds.zig` implementing Fractal Neural Dynamic System or similar subsystem, describing dynamic fractal-based neural network behavior.

Implement `formal_verification.zig` containing runtime checks and assertions, maintaining connection between formal proofs and running code.

Implement `ibm_quantum.zig` providing interface to IBM quantum computers or simulators, enabling real quantum hardware usage for certain computations.

Implement `mod.zig` as module definition file organizing and exporting library functions.

Implement `nsir_core.zig` implementing Neural-Symbolic Intermediate Representation core, bridging neural networks and symbolic logic.

Implement `quantum_logic.zig` providing software simulation of quantum logic gates and operations, enabling quantum algorithm execution on conventional hardware.

Implement `quantum_task_adapter.zig` adapting tasks to quantum-compatible format, scheduling tasks to quantum processor or simulator.

Implement `r_gpu.zig` implementing Relational GPU or Remote GPU functions, defining special GPU operations for graph-based computations.

Implement `reasoning_orchestrator.zig` controlling high-level reasoning processes, deciding which logical or neural module to use for problem solving.

Implement `signal_propagation.zig` simulating signal propagation in neural networks or knowledge graphs, managing activation levels and information flow.

Implement `surprise_memory.zig` implementing special memory module handling "surprise" or unexpected information, highlighting anomalies for learning.

Implement `temporal_graph.zig` implementing graph data structure handling temporal changes, enabling tracking of knowledge base history and temporal reasoning.

Implement `type_theory.zig` implementing type-theoretical rules in Zig code, checking semantic correctness at runtime.

Implement `verified_inference_engine.zig` implementing inference engine where every step is mathematically proven, drawing only logically guaranteed conclusions.

Implement `vpu.zig` controlling Vision Processing Unit or Vector Processing Unit, handling hardware specialized for image or vector data processing.

Implement `z_runtime.zig` providing custom Zig runtime extensions and settings, handling system startup, exceptions, and global state.

Implement `zk_verification.zig` generating and verifying zero-knowledge proofs, enabling verification of private computation correctness without data disclosure.

Implement `esso_optimizer.zig` implementing Entangled Stochastic Symmetry Optimizer, a quantum-inspired optimization algorithm seeking stable graph states.

Implement `quantum_hardware.zig` providing physical or simulated quantum hardware interface, handling qubits, gates, and measurements at low level.

Implement `security_proofs.zig` implementing and checking security guarantees, ensuring cryptographic compliance.

Implement `chaos_core.zig` implementing Chaos Core Kernel, a self-organizing entropy-monitoring system kernel managing resources and stability dynamically.

### Specialized Subsystems

Implement `index/ssi.zig` providing concrete Self-Similar Index implementation, performing fractal-structure indexing for fast search.

Implement `optimizer/sfd.zig` implementing Stochastic Fractal Dimension-based optimization algorithm, using dimension calculation for parameter space mapping.

Implement `ranker/ranker.zig` implementing ranking module for results or inferences, determining most relevant information.

Implement `zk/inference_trace.circom` describing inference process zero-knowledge circuit in Circom language, enabling proof of model execution without revealing the model.

### WebAssembly Support

Implement `wasm/wasm_bindings.zig` providing WebAssembly bindings, enabling browser or Wasm environment execution.

Implement `bench_deps.zig` and `wasm_deps.zig` defining dependencies for benchmarking and WebAssembly builds.

### Entry Points

Implement `main.zig` as standard execution entry point, initializing components and starting main loop.

Implement `main_gpu.zig` as GPU-accelerated version entry point, setting up GPU environment and CUDA/ROCm context at startup.

Implement `main_distributed.zig` as distributed system entry point, configuring network and inter-node communication.

Implement `main_distributed_futhark.zig` as Futhark-based distributed system launcher, connecting Futhark kernels with distributed logic.

### Testing and Quality Assurance

Implement `tests/stress_tensor_refcount.zig` as stress test for tensor reference counting mechanism under extreme load.

Implement `tokenizer/mgt.zig` implementing Multi-Granularity Tokenizer at character, word, and morpheme levels.

### Automation Scripts

Implement `scripts/bootstrap_verification_libs.sh` automatically installing verification environment (Agda, Lean, etc.) and downloading mathematical libraries.

Implement `scripts/verify_all.sh` controlling complete verification process, running all proofs and tests sequentially with reporting.

Implement `scripts/fpga_synthesis.sh` automating FPGA synthesis process, compiling HDL code to bitstreams.

Implement `scripts/profile_edge_fractal.sh` profiling fractal computation performance, measuring runtime and resource requirements.

Implement `scripts/run_profiling.sh` providing general profiling for system performance analysis, collecting CPU, memory, and GPU usage metrics.

Implement `verify_all.sh` launching all verification processes (Agda, Lean, TLA+, etc.) with single command, automating complete system checking for CI/CD pipelines.

### Server Infrastructure

Implement `inference_server.zig` as HTTP or RPC server serving inference requests, enabling remote access and integration.

### Hardware Description - ASIC

Implement `asic/floorplan.tcl` describing ASIC chip physical layout as Tcl script, defining transistor and wire positions on silicon.

Implement `asic/synthesis.tcl` controlling logic synthesis for ASIC design, translating Verilog code to gate level according to manufacturing technology rules.

### Hardware Description - FPGA

Implement `fpga/constraints.pcf` containing FPGA pin assignments and timing constraints.

Implement `fpga/top_level.v` as top-level Verilog module for FPGA design, integrating all submodules and defining chip external interfaces.

### Fuzz Testing

Implement `fuzz/fuzz_memory.zig` fuzzing memory manager with chaotic operations to find crashes.

Implement `fuzz/fuzz_ssi.zig` fuzzing SSI indexer with random data testing fault tolerance.

Implement `fuzz/fuzz_tensor.zig` fuzzing tensor operations with random matrices testing numerical stability.

### Hardware Acceleration - Futhark

Implement `accel/futhark_kernels.fut` containing GPU-written Futhark kernels including matrix multiplication, reductions, and parallelizable algorithms.

Implement `accel/main.fut` as Futhark program entry point, integrating kernels and defining GPU program inputs/outputs.

Implement `accel/futhark_bindings.zig` containing Futhark-generated C/Zig bindings, enabling compiled GPU code invocation from main Zig program.

Implement `accel/cuda_bindings.zig` providing direct bindings to NVIDIA CUDA library for low-level GPU control and memory management.

Implement `accel/accel_interface.zig` providing unified interface for different accelerators (GPU, FPGA, ASIC), hiding hardware-specific details.

Implement `accel/fractal_lpu.zig` implementing software emulation or controller for Fractal Language Processing Unit, hardware-accelerating fractal-based language processing.

Implement `accel/futhark_kernels.c` as Futhark compiler-generated C code that Zig program actually invokes and links.

### Hardware Description - RTL (Haskell/Clash)

Implement `rtl/MemoryArbiter.hs` describing hardware logic controlling memory access using Haskell-based Clash, deciding memory access during conflicts.

Implement `rtl/RankerCore.hs` describing ranker unit hardware in Haskell/Clash, implementing relevance calculation algorithm at circuit level.

Implement `rtl/SSISearch.hs` describing SSI search unit hardware model in Haskell, performing graph traversal directly in hardware bypassing CPU.

All implementations must be complete, production-ready code with no placeholders, mock implementations, or simplifications. Every module must include complete error handling, edge case management, proper memory management, comprehensive documentation, and integration with all dependent modules. The formal verification proofs must be complete and mechanically checkable. The hardware descriptions must be synthesizable to actual hardware. All interfaces between components must be fully specified and implemented. The system must compile, verify, and execute without modification.
